_comment: Editorial picks for the website. Ids are site-data entry ids (see scripts/export_site_data.py); the export fails if an id is not a listed entry. Featured is an editorial choice, never paid placement.

featured.label: Featured
featured.note: Cited answers to clinical questions for healthcare professionals, researched from clinical guidelines and peer-reviewed literature.

collections.title: Personal health
collections.intro: Connectors that work on your own health data: records and labs, wearables and sleep, glucose and nutrition, training and symptoms. Hand-picked from the index. Informational only, not medical advice.

collections.title: Research & writing
collections.intro: Connectors for finding current sources, reading documents and transcripts, organizing notes, and preparing written work. Choose the tools that fit where your sources and drafts already live. Check original sources and citations before sharing; review permissions before connecting private files.

collections.title: Everyday planning
collections.intro: Connectors for organizing a week: calendars and family schedules, tasks and habits, meals and groceries, and trips and days out. Choose the tools that fit the services you already use; account requirements and local coverage vary. Review permissions before connecting personal accounts, and confirm dates, prices, availability and any changes or purchases before proceeding.

collections.title: Learning & study
collections.intro: Connectors for finding course material and scholarly sources, exploring concepts, turning notes into review questions, and keeping study knowledge organized. Choose the tools that fit your subjects and existing study habits; some require an account or access through an organization. Check explanations and generated answers against original material, follow your school or course rules on AI use, and review permissions before connecting private notes or files.

collections.title: Vibe coders / non-SWEs
collections.intro: Connectors for people building apps by conversation rather than writing most of the code themselves: prompt-based builders, design and app services, hosting, and checks on what shipped. Pick the services your project already uses; these are alternatives and supporting tools, not a stack you need to install in full. Account requirements and charges vary. Review changes, permissions and costs before approving actions, test with non-production data, and get an experienced engineer to review authentication, access controls and sensitive-data handling before a public launch.

collections.title: Software engineers
collections.intro: Connectors for engineers working directly with code, tests and production systems: repository search and current documentation, change planning, API and browser testing, delivery pipelines, infrastructure, security checks and incident investigation. Choose tools that match your existing engineering stack. Review generated changes and test results rather than treating them as approval to ship; use least-privilege access, keep secrets out of prompts, and confirm migrations, infrastructure changes and production actions before execution.
